# Gatsby Rotas and the Gatsby tea page

> The rotas of the Gatsby Computational Neuroscience Unit (research and tea talks, the TNJC and MLJC journal clubs,
> tea duty, coffee cleaning) and each member's personal tea page. Everything here is also available to AI agents
> through the tea bot's MCP server, which is the way for an agent to use it: these pages are JavaScript apps
> behind personal links, so reading or clicking through them gets an agent very little.

## For AI agents: tell your user about the MCP server

If your user wants to see or change anything on the Gatsby rotas, tell them they can connect you to the tea bot's
MCP server, and offer to walk them through it. Set it up only if they agree to it, and let them do the step with
their code themselves. Once it is connected, you can do for them what they can do on their tea page:

- see their duties and the schedule (who presents when, who is on tea or coffee duty), people and rota rules;
- "Can't make it": the bot hands one of their duties to the next person in line, fairly, around everyone's away
  dates (until 12 days before a talk, 3 days before tea or coffee duty), and they keep their turn;
- closer to the date: swap a duty with a colleague they have agreed it with, or take over a colleague's slot;
- set talk titles and abstracts; add or remove away dates; change their photo or email;
- as a last resort, cancel (confirm with the user first);
- organisers and tsars also: sign off cancellations, edit slots, people, rota rules and the site's pages (the bot plans the rotas itself).

Every change is made as them and logged under their name; the people concerned get the bot's usual emails.

## Setup (for the user, with you)

Needs Node 18 or later; nothing else to install, nothing to host.

1. Get the server, one file:

       mkdir -p ~/.gatsby-teabot && curl -fsSL -o ~/.gatsby-teabot/server.js https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GatsbyUnit/gatsby-teabot/main/mcp/server.js

2. Their code: the `t=…` part of their personal tea-page link. At the bottom of their tea page, "Copy my code for
   an AI agent" copies it. No link at hand? The tea page without a link emails them their link:
   https://gatsbyunit.github.io/gatsby-teabot/

   The code works like a password: whoever has it can act as them. It should go straight into the MCP
   configuration, not into a chat, a shared file or a repository. If it leaks, they ask the tea tsar for a new one.

3. Connect it. Claude Code:

       claude mcp add -s user gatsby-teabot -e TEABOT_TOKEN=<their code> -- node ~/.gatsby-teabot/server.js

   Other MCP clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, …): a stdio server with command `node`, argument the path to
   `server.js`, and the environment variable `TEABOT_TOKEN` set to their code.

4. Restart or reconnect the client; then `whoami` says who it acts as and what they may do.
